issues.description: SealSaloon constructor signature is inconsistent with the specification: the problem statement/UML requires a public constructor `SealSaloon(String)` (saloon name), but the solution implements only a no-argument constructor `SealSaloon()`. Students following the spec will implement a String-parameter constructor, while tests (or the reference) may rely on the other signature, causing compilation/test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Implement `public SealSaloon(String name)` as required (store `name` in a private field with a getter if needed). Optionally keep `public SealSaloon()` as an overload delegating to `this("")`, but ensure the String constructor exists and is used in examples/tests.

issues.description: Contradiction within the problem statement about `stock`: the UML shows `stock` as a normal instance attribute/association of `SealSaloon`, but the text explicitly requires `stock` to be static (shared across all SealSaloon instances). This creates ambiguity about whether each saloon has its own stock or all share one.
issues.suggestedFix: Align UML and text: either (a) mark `stock` as `{static}`/underlined in the UML and keep the text as-is, or (b) remove the static requirement from the text and adjust tests accordingly.

issues.description: Stock API differs from the UML: the UML lists only `add`, `take`, `findStockIngredient`, `addToStockIngredients`, and `emptyStock`, but both template and solution expose an additional public mutator `setStockIngredients(StockIngredient[])`. This expands the public API beyond the spec and can mislead students about what methods they are expected/allowed to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Either add `setStockIngredients(StockIngredient[])` to the UML/spec (if intended for setup/testing) or remove it from template/solution and rely on `addToStockIngredients(...)`/`emptyStock()` for stock management.
